utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That area, it was a corner, the very corner of a parking lot, and it was surrounded on three sides by buildings that were -- that were six-storey buildings. And on the fourth side, there was Mojmilo, the Mount Mojmilo, and that was an open area. So it was not possible to see it at all and not to observe it from any point whatsoever. We would not be discovered if we were having fun, if we were relaxing, if we were playing a football game.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, about how far from the nearest confrontation line between the two armies in the conflict was that football field or football pitch?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC
utterances.text: The confrontation line was at about 130 metres from us away. So Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the length of a parking lot, the length of two streets or a green area. So the street is Partizanskih Olimpijada, and then the last buildings that had unpaired numbers -- in pair numbers, odd numbers. And on the Serbian side, it was the Indira Gandhi Street. So only 30 metres away. The soldiers could even shout at each other and talk by speaking out loud.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, were there spectators for this football game?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where were they located?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC
utterances.text: Let me just explain: When we talk about these cars, these old cars that were overturned, the APCs that would arrive along the Lukavica Road, they would shell all the cars that were parked. And those cars were then -- would become used cars, old cars. And this is how we delineated the football pitch, because we put these cars there, and we had turned the wheels towards the football pitch. That's how we placed these cars so that the children -- maybe there was about a hundred young people on these vehicles, from 10 to 15 years of age. I don't know for sure. I couldn't tell you their exact age. And on the other side, there were the spectators, a few women, from 50 to a hundred people also were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the apartment buildings which surrounded the pitch on three sides, as you explained to us, were there people there?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the balconies of these apartment buildings, there were people. There were women, children, men, and they were observing the football match. They were watching us play.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, the people on the ground in the vicinity of the football pitch, those spectators who were on the cars or around the football pitch itself, were they in uniform or not, or did you see anyone among them in uniform or did you not see anyone in uniform?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC
utterances.text: No. Let me explain. This was a sports activity. We wanted to relax a little bit. No one amongst the present people did not wear any sign indicating a uniform, not even a uniform indicating that they were members of any police force. Now, it was possible that some of them may have been either police officer or a military man, but these people were wearing civilian clothes. Now, as for the players who were playing ball and myself, we were wearing either jogging outfits or sports outfits. That's how we were dressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. And the -- did you notice anybody there that morning with any arms or weapons?

utterances.speaker: ISMET FAZLIC
utterances.text: No. There were passages. Because there was sniping activity coming from all sides of Dobrinja, for the village of Zepa, from the church bell tower, from all the sides, there were some passages. And these passages and the trenches and some basements that had holes through the street, APG, through the odd numbers and even numbers, the army was going on the front lines through Partizanskih Brigada Street through those passages.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, let's get back to the football game, if we may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, we continued for another seven minutes. If you're changing subjects, I'd rather have the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic, I know that you have been in this Court for only a very short time and your examination will continue tomorrow. So we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
